title: Coleman integration, Part II: harmonic realizations, integration indices and descent
summary: Extend good-reduction Coleman integration by all-prime natural single integration in arbitrary reduction, harmonic curve realizations, double/triple indices, corrected pairings and trace/divisor descent.

layers.title: Finite graph cochains and harmonic normalization

targets.name: Graph.LengthCochains
targets.statement: For a finite graph Γ, retain both flags of every edge, including a loop, and an orientation-reversing fixed-point-free involution e ↦ −e on its darts. For a field k of characteristic zero and positive rational lengths ℓ(e)=ℓ(−e), define C⁰=V→k, C¹={c:E→k | c(−e)=−c(e)}, d f(e)=f(tail e)−f(head e), div_ℓ(c)(v)=Σ_{tail(e)=v} c(e)/ℓ(e), Harm_ℓ=ker(div_ℓ), and (c,d)_ℓ=Σ_{E/±} c(e)d(e)/ℓ(e). These are modules, linear maps, a submodule and a bilinear form on the native graph carrier; the flag presentation has an explicit forgetful comparison to Graph.IsLink.
hypotheses: Γ has finite actual vertex and edge sets; ambient types need not be finite
k is a field with CharZero
ℓ(e) is a strictly positive rational number, interpreted through ℚ→k

locator.where: Definitions 4.1–4.3, printed pp. 11–12, besser2017 line 528; rational-length extension by subdivision from Proposition 4.12(3), besser2017 line 768

api.name: LengthCochains.mk
api.statement: A native graph, a choice of its two flags per edge and positive reversal-invariant rational lengths give this presentation; reversing the chosen orientation gives a canonically isomorphic complex.

api.name: LengthCochains.ext
api.statement: Two cochains are equal exactly when their values on every dart agree; values on one dart of each edge suffice.

api.name: LengthCochains.div_d_adjoint
api.statement: Σ_v f(v) div_ℓ(c)(v)=(d f,c)_ℓ; loops contribute two opposite values.

api.name: LengthCochains.map
api.statement: Graph isomorphisms preserving lengths and characteristic-zero coefficient embeddings commute with d, divergence and the edge pairing; unit lengths recover Definitions 4.1–4.3.

api.name: LengthCochains.simple_laplacian
api.statement: For a finite simple graph with unit lengths, div(d f) is SimpleGraph.lapMatrix acting on f. The multigraph extension retains parallel edges and two loop flags.

api.name: LengthCochains.simpleCochainsEquiv
api.statement: For a finite simple graph G and characteristic-zero field k, the identity on dart values identifies C¹ with Additive (G.oneCochains (Multiplicative k)). Give the latter its pointwise k-module structure. Under this k-linear equivalence d f is the negative of the additive translation of G.coboundary (Multiplicative k) (Multiplicative.ofAdd ∘ f). Thus the identity on C⁰ and the negative of this equivalence on C¹ is a chain comparison. Coefficient maps and graph relabelling are the supplied maps through this bridge.

tests.name: Graph.LengthCochains_1
tests.statement: On one oriented edge v→w with f(v)=2,f(w)=5, this roadmap has d f=−3; the additive value of the pinned coboundary on Multiplicative.ofAdd ∘ f is +3. Negating the degree-one comparison makes the chain square commute.

tests.name: Graph.LengthCochains_2
tests.statement: For one vertex and no edges C¹=0 and Harm_ℓ=0; the empty graph has C⁰=C¹=0.

tests.name: Graph.LengthCochains_3
tests.statement: A loop at v carrying c(e)=1,c(−e)=−1 has divergence zero and is a nonzero harmonic cochain. Giving the loop only one dart incorrectly excludes it.

tests.name: LengthCochains_pairing_weight
tests.statement: On one edge of length 1/2, c=2,d=3 give (c,d)_ℓ=12; using an unweighted product gives 6.

tests.name: LengthCochains_pairing_reverse
tests.statement: Reversing the selected orientation replaces both c,d by their negatives and leaves the value 12. A zero argument gives zero.

tests.name: LengthCochains_divergence_bridge
tests.statement: For one edge of length 1/2 with c=2, divergence is +4 at its tail and −4 at its head; it is not harmonic. An outgoing sum omitting the inverse length gives the wrong values.

tests.name: LengthCochains_cochain_antisymmetry
tests.statement: A cochain assigning 1 to both directions of a nonloop edge is not in C¹ in characteristic zero. On no edges C¹ is the zero module; on one loop C¹ is k.

tests.name: LengthCochains_degree_zero
tests.statement: The empty graph has only the zero 0-cochain; on one isolated vertex C⁰=k and d=0. On two isolated vertices its kernel has two independent constants.

targets.proofSketch: Use submodules of function modules and finite sums. Define the two flags separately even when their incident vertices coincide; the involution has no fixed dart. The adjoint identity follows by grouping the two flags of each edge.
targets.title: Cochains with edge identities

targets.name: Graph.harmonic_exact_decomposition
targets.statement: For Γ,k,ℓ as in §1.1, C¹=Harm_ℓ ⊕ im(d). Thus every graph cohomology class has one harmonic representative. The kernel of d consists of the functions constant on each connected component. If Γ is connected and nonempty, a potential for the exact part is unique modulo one common constant. Harmonic and exact cochains are orthogonal for ( , )_ℓ; the induced form on harmonic cochains is nondegenerate. All these decompositions commute with coefficient extension.
hypotheses: The hypotheses of §1.1; connectedness and nonemptiness only for a single common constant

locator.where: Theorem 4.4 and following orthogonality statement, p. 12, besser2017 line 553; rational-length consequence

api.name: harmonicProjection
api.statement: The unique harmonic projection C¹→ₗ[k]Harm_ℓ has kernel im(d), is identity on Harm_ℓ and is idempotent.

api.name: harmonicProjection_changePotential
api.statement: harmonicProjection(c+d a)=harmonicProjection(c).

api.name: rationalLaplacian_rank
api.statement: For each connected component with r vertices, the rational weighted Laplacian has rank r−1, preserved over k.

api.name: harmonicProjection_simpleCohomologyEquiv
api.statement: The value-preserving cochain equivalence of §1.1 sends im(d) onto the additive translation of the pinned coboundary range, since negation preserves that range. Transport scalar multiplication to Additive (G.FirstCohomology (Multiplicative k)); the induced quotient equivalence is k-linear and identifies harmonic representatives with this existing quotient. Import FirstCohomology.lift, mk_eq_mk_iff, firstCohomologyMap and firstCohomologyRelabel through the bridge; do not redefine their simple-graph universal properties or functoriality.

tests.name: Graph.harmonic_exact_decomposition_1
tests.statement: On a cyclic triangle with unit lengths and cyclic edge values (3,0,0), the harmonic part is (1,1,1) and the exact part is (2,−1,−1).

tests.name: Graph.harmonic_exact_decomposition_2
tests.statement: On a tree the harmonic part is zero; on two isolated vertices the ambiguity is two constants, not one.

tests.name: Graph.harmonic_exact_decomposition_3
tests.statement: In characteristic 3 on a triangle, the constant cyclic cochain (1,1,1) is both exact and harmonic. Characteristic zero is essential; p=3 coefficients ℚ₃ are still allowed.

tests.name: harmonic_simple_bridge
tests.statement: On a simple triangle the cochain (1,1,1) has nonzero cycle class in both quotients; on a one-edge tree ±3 are coboundaries in both. The quotient bridge preserves cochain values, while the signed chain comparison negates them.

targets.proofSketch: Over ℚ, the adjoint identity identifies the Laplacian kernel after embedding into ℝ: Σ_edges (f(v)−f(w))²/ℓ=0 forces componentwise constants. A maximal minor is a nonzero rational, so the same rank holds over every characteristic-zero k. Rank-nullity and orthogonality give the direct sum, uniqueness, nondegeneracy and extension compatibility.
targets.title: The harmonic representative

targets.name: Graph.harmonic_subdivision
targets.statement: If an edge of length ℓ is subdivided into consecutive positive rational lengths ℓ_i with Σℓ_i=ℓ, a harmonic jump c on that edge extends by c_i=(ℓ_i/ℓ)c. Restriction adds the jumps along the chain, and these operations identify graph cohomology and its harmonic representatives. Pairings ( , )_ℓ are preserved when both arguments are extended this way. If a residue current r is constant along the chain, Σ_i c_i r=c r. Attaching a tree contributes zero harmonic current. Uniform subdivision into m pieces gives c/m on each new edge, for m≥1.
hypotheses: Finite graphs and positive rational lengths as in §1.1
m is positive; no division by zero
New degree-two vertices have no additional attached marked source terms

locator.where: Corollary 1.2 and preceding subdivision argument, p. 3, besser-zerbes2017 line 99; compare besser2017 Proposition 4.12(3), line 768

api.name: harmonic_subdivision_comp
api.statement: Successive subdivisions give the same extension as their common refinement.

api.name: harmonic_subdivision_residue
api.statement: The jump-residue contribution is invariant under subdivision; reversing every dart preserves it.

tests.name: Graph.harmonic_subdivision_1
tests.statement: Splitting a jump 6 into lengths 1/3 and 2/3 of its original length gives jumps 2 and 4, total 6.

tests.name: Graph.harmonic_subdivision_2
tests.statement: m=1 is identity; a rational tail carries zero current.

tests.name: Graph.harmonic_subdivision_3
tests.statement: For a triangle with jumps (1,1,1), dividing one edge into two halves gives (1/2,1/2) on that edge. Treating all four resulting lengths as 1 changes the harmonic representative and is not the same metric realization.

targets.proofSketch: Divergence at each new vertex forces constant c_i/ℓ_i. Summing along the chain determines that current. Direct substitution proves the energy and residue identities; the cohomology isomorphism follows by extending potentials and applying §1.2.
targets.title: Subdivision with a fixed metric

layers.title: Logarithmic annular functions and the double index

targets.name: Annulus.residueTransport
targets.title: Residues, finite maps and meromorphic germs
targets.statement: Extend the supplied annular residue to differential-compatible finite maps of oriented open annuli: for a finite map of positive oriented degree n, Res(φ*ω)=n Res(ω). Reversal changes the sign. Residue commutes with finite separable coefficient extension, coefficient trace and restriction to smaller end annuli. At a smooth closed point x of a curve over a characteristic-zero field, a uniformizer identifies its completed local ring with κ(x)[[z]] and its meromorphic differential germs with κ(x)((z))dz; residue is coefficient −1. For a meromorphic differential converging on a punctured disc, its formal and analytic residues agree. There is no map from every analytic annular Laurent family to a bounded-below formal Laurent series.
hypotheses: Formal coefficients are characteristic-zero fields; analytic coefficients are complete nontrivially normed ultrametric fields
A finite analytic map has positive degree and compatible orientation; coefficient trace is for finite separable extensions
Formal/analytic germ comparison requires a meromorphic germ with finitely many negative powers

locator.where: Definition 3.1 and (3.1), p. 9, besser2017 line 402; degree consequence as in besser-dejeu2012 Lemma 8.1, p. 361, line 2529

api.name: residueTransport_degree
api.statement: Res of the pullback of dz/z under z=t^n is n.

api.name: residueTransport_germ
api.statement: Meromorphic point expansions preserve differentiation, residue, finite scalar extension and the two compatible residue computations.

tests.name: Annulus.residueTransport_check1
tests.statement: For z=t² the residue of dz/z is 2; for z=t⁻¹ it is −1 in the t orientation.

tests.name: Annulus.residueTransport_check2
tests.statement: The identity map gives residue 1 on dz/z; constants have derivative residue zero. A constant map is excluded from the positive-degree claim.

tests.name: Annulus.residueTransport_check3
tests.statement: At a quadratic closed point a residue 1 traces to 2. An analytic Laurent family with infinitely many negative terms is not a formal Laurent germ.

targets.proofSketch: Use the supplied coefficient residue and restriction. Factor a finite annular map locally as a monomial times a unit, apply the logarithmic derivative and the exact-residue law, and extend by the residue/exact decomposition. Formal substitution is coefficientwise. The smooth completed-local-ring parameter theorem gives point expansions; the finite negative part makes the analytic/formal comparison legitimate. Coefficient extraction commutes with linear trace.

targets.name: Annulus.LogarithmicFunctions
targets.statement: For a characteristic-zero field k define the formal extension A_log=k((z))[L], dL=dz/z, and its degree-at-most-one subspace A_log,1=k((z))+kL. In the analytic case take the degree-at-most-one subspace O_k(A)+kL inside the supplied AnnulusLogRing on an open annulus over a complete subfield of ℂ_p, with its fixed logarithm realization. This subspace, its coefficient decomposition and the index data are the additions here; the analytic polynomial ring, its derivation, changeParam, primitive existence and constant kernel are imported. The formal derivative maps A_log,1 onto k((z))dz with kernel k, and Res(d(f+aL))=a. The analytic version has the same residue criterion using the supplied primitive theorem. The extension to general complete ultrametric characteristic-zero analytic coefficients is §2.1a.
hypotheses: Formal k is a characteristic-zero field
Analytic imported case: k a complete subfield of ℂ_p, A a genuine open annulus or end germ, branch as in ColemanIntegration L0.20
A common branch for realization and orientation with Res(dz/z)=1; all restrictions share a convergence domain

locator.where: Definition 3.1, pp. 9–10, besser2017 line 402; formal polynomial logarithms in besser-dejeu2012 §7, pp. 355–356, line 2232

api.name: LogarithmicFunctions.mk
api.statement: Construct f+aL from an analytic or formal Laurent f and scalar a; add, scale, differentiate and restrict coefficientwise.

api.name: LogarithmicFunctions.ext
api.statement: Equality in a fixed parameter is equality of the Laurent part and the coefficient a.

api.name: LogarithmicFunctions.residue_zero_iff
api.statement: F is Laurent without L exactly when Res(dF)=0.

api.name: LogarithmicFunctions.changeParameter
api.statement: On the analytic subspace restrict the supplied AnnulusLogRing.changeParam, retaining u=az(1+h), |a|=1 and |h|<1. Formally, for u=az(1+h), a≠0 and h∈zk[[z]], choose a scalar δ and transport L_u=L_z+δ+log(1+h) through the full differential-algebra substitution. The broader analytic coefficient/radius-transport statement is §2.1a. Orientation reversal changes both residue and the logarithmic generator.

tests.name: Annulus.LogarithmicFunctions_1
tests.statement: d(2+3L)=3 dz/z and Res=3; replacing the residue by the constant term of F fails.

tests.name: Annulus.LogarithmicFunctions_2
tests.statement: dC=0 for every constant C and dL≠0, including over ℚ₂.

tests.name: Annulus.LogarithmicFunctions_3
tests.statement: L² is in A_log but not A_log,1, since d(L²)=2L dz/z is not an analytic differential. Characteristic p would also make d(z^p)=0.

targets.proofSketch: Use Polynomial (LaurentSeries k) for the formal ring, with dL=z⁻¹. Integrate formal monomials by nonzero integer denominators; residues prove the direct-sum decomposition and constant kernel. On the supplied analytic ring take the degree-one subspace and use exists_logLaurent_primitive and logLaurent_derivative_eq_zero_iff; do not reconstruct analytic integration. The formal and analytic carriers are compared only for convergent meromorphic germs, via §2.0.
targets.title: Functions with one logarithmic term

targets.name: AnnulusLogRing.generalCoefficients
targets.title: The analytic coefficient extension
targets.statement: For every complete nontrivially normed ultrametric characteristic-zero field k and genuine open annulus A, extend the supplied polynomial-logarithm differential algebra to O_k(A)[L], dL=dz/z, using the supplied LaurentOn carrier. Its differential is surjective onto O_k(A)[L]dz and its kernel is k. Its degree-at-most-one part has image Ω¹(A). Restriction, isometric coefficient extension and differential-compatible parameter substitution commute with these operations. For complete subfields of ℂ_p identify this algebra with the supplied AnnulusLogRing, including its changeParam under the supplied unit/small-perturbation hypotheses; do not reconstruct that special case. Pointwise realization is asserted only when a compatible logarithm branch and a faithful analytic evaluation are supplied.
hypotheses: k complete, nontrivially normed, ultrametric and characteristic zero
A is an open annulus with nonempty interval of positive radii; restrictions stay in a common domain
Parameter change u=az(1+h) has a≠0 and |h|<1 on the domain, transports radii, and includes a chosen logarithm δ of a

locator.where: Definition 3.1, p. 9, besser2017 line 404; polynomial-log extension of besser-dejeu2012 §7, p. 355, line 2232

api.name: generalCoefficients_primitive
api.statement: Every logarithmic polynomial differential has a primitive, unique modulo k.

api.name: generalCoefficients_base
api.statement: For complete subfields of ℂ_p these maps agree with exists_logLaurent_primitive, logLaurent_derivative_eq_zero_iff and AnnulusLogRing.changeParam.

tests.name: AnnulusLogRing.generalCoefficients_check1
tests.statement: d(L²/2)=L dz/z also over ℚ₂, and d(L³/3)=L² dz/z over ℚ₃.

tests.name: AnnulusLogRing.generalCoefficients_check2
tests.statement: A scalar has zero derivative; L and every nonconstant Laurent monomial do not. Characteristic p would make z^p a counterexample.

tests.name: AnnulusLogRing.generalCoefficients_check3
tests.statement: For u=az with chosen δ, L_u maps to L_z+δ. On a closed annulus boundary, division by integers can lose convergence; openness is required.

targets.proofSketch: Reuse the supplied Laurent coefficient algebra. The ultrametric absolute value restricted to ℚ bounds inverse integers by a fixed power of their real size. An interior-radius margin absorbs this growth. Integrate by parts in L, and prove the kernel coefficientwise by descending degree and the residue obstruction. This is the general-coefficient extension of the supplied analytic theorem; the formal argument stays in §2.1.

targets.name: Annulus.doubleIndex
targets.statement: For the oriented formal punctured disc or open annulus of §2.1 define B_e(f+aL,g+bL)=Res_e(f dg)+b Res_e(f dz/z)−a Res_e(g dz/z), using a parameter compatible with the orientation. This is the unique alternating k-bilinear pairing with B_e(F,G)=Res_e(F dG) when F has no logarithmic term. In particular B_e(C,G)=C Res_e(dG). This definition owns the index; analytic residue is imported and its additional transport/germ laws are §2.0.
hypotheses: The field, function spaces, orientation and branch hypotheses of §2.1

locator.where: Definition 3.2 and Lemma 3.3, p. 9, besser2017 line 421; besser-dejeu2012 Definition 7.1 and construction, p. 356, line 2243

api.name: doubleIndex_ext
api.statement: An alternating bilinear pairing with the analytic-first residue rule equals B_e.

api.name: doubleIndex_add_left
api.statement: B_e(F+F′,G)=B_e(F,G)+B_e(F′,G), with analogous scalar and right-variable laws.

api.name: doubleIndex_add_constants
api.statement: B_e(F+A,G+B)−B_e(F,G)=A Res_e(dG)−B Res_e(dF).

tests.name: Annulus.doubleIndex_1
tests.statement: B_e(1,L)=1, B_e(L,1)=−1 and B_e(z,z⁻¹)=−1; both residue order and logarithmic constant terms are detected.

tests.name: Annulus.doubleIndex_2
tests.statement: B_e(L,L)=0 and B_e(C,D)=0 for constants C,D; the expression Res(F dG) alone is undefined when F=L.

tests.name: Annulus.doubleIndex_3
tests.statement: If a=0 the formula is Res(f dG); if b=0 it is −Res(g dF). These agree when both are Laurent because Res d(fg)=0.

targets.proofSketch: Expand in the direct sum of the Laurent subspace and kL. Residues of exact Laurent differentials vanish, proving alternation. The residue rule determines all terms except B(L,L), which is zero by alternation.
targets.title: The alternating local index

targets.name: Annulus.doubleIndex_pullback
targets.statement: Let φ:e′→e be a finite map of annuli with positive degree n and compatible orientation, or a formal parameter substitution of ramification order n. For pulled-back functions and branch, B_e′(φ*F,φ*G)=n B_e(F,G). In particular the index is invariant under orientation-preserving parameter isomorphisms, and reverses sign with orientation. Scalar extension commutes with B; restricting to smaller annuli preserves B. For a finite separable coefficient extension L/k, the residue trace commutes with Laurent coefficient trace.
hypotheses: The hypotheses of §2.1
φ finite of positive degree with no poles in its analytic domain; formal substitution has positive order
Branches and coefficient embeddings agree on the source field

locator.where: Definition 7.1, p. 356, line 2243; §8 and residue-degree argument in Lemma 8.1, p. 361, line 2524; double-index consequence

api.name: doubleIndex_scalarExtension
api.statement: The embedded value of B_k(F,G) equals B_L(F_L,G_L).

api.name: doubleIndex_shrink
api.statement: Analytic continuation to a common end annulus identifies the values.

tests.name: Annulus.doubleIndex_pullback_2

tests.name: Annulus.doubleIndex_pullback_3

targets.proofSketch: Apply the residue pullback law of §2.0 to the analytic-first rule; uniqueness in §2.2 supplies all logarithmic terms. Coefficient trace commutes with coefficient extraction. The same argument handles shrinking and scalar extension.

layers.title: Wide-open pairings and semistable graph corrections

targets.name: Semistable.colemanCover
targets.title: Coleman domains of a nodal model
targets.statement: For a split regular nodal model of a smooth proper geometrically connected curve over finite K/ℚ_p, construct the component wide opens, their smooth residue domains, paired end annuli and restriction maps for forms. After separating pole sections and making a compatible finite extension and regular subdivision for self-nodes when necessary, compare each component core and a cofinal system of strict neighborhoods with a Coleman good-reduction wide-open presentation. Transfer the supplied Coleman algebra and integration through these identifications; coordinate changes preserve germs and primitive constants. The overlap differential equations give constant differences of two Coleman primitives on a connecting annulus. This constructs no restriction of a natural primitive.
hypotheses: p any prime; K/ℚ_p finite; model split, regular and nodal
Finite pole support is separated from nodes and connecting annuli
Use cofinal strict neighborhoods and compatible refinements; a self-node is subdivided before choosing Coleman domains
All cover assertions are over the chosen realization field; refinements compare in a common finite extension

locator.where: §4, pp. 12–13, besser2017 line 562; besser-zerbes2017 §1, pp. 1–2, lines 49–85

api.name: colemanCover_restrict
api.statement: Ordinary and paired-end restrictions commute with d and the supplied Coleman realization on common strict neighborhoods.

api.name: colemanCover_refinement
api.statement: Subdivisions give compatible Coleman domains; forgetting inserted domains adds the jumps along the chain.

tests.statement: A smooth special fibre has one core and no connecting ends; its presentation is the supplied good-reduction one.

tests.name: Semistable.colemanCover_check2

tests.name: Semistable.colemanCover_check3

targets.proofSketch: Use the formal tubes of the smooth affine component cores and their good-reduction lifts, compare their cofinal strict neighborhoods, and glue the nodal charts along annuli. Import Coleman pullback only where its same-reduction and common-Frobenius-power bounds hold. Integration and the constant kernel transfer through those comparisons; §1.3 handles coarsening.

targets.name: ColemanWideOpen.fullAnalyticExtension
targets.title: Full analytic Coleman coefficients
targets.statement: For a geometrically connected Coleman wide open U with finite end set, extend the supplied good-reduction dagger Coleman algebra to the actual Coleman function and one-form algebra with full analytic coefficients on U over ℂ_p. Construct its derivation, analytic-function inclusion, products, integration of Coleman one-forms modulo constants, and differential-compatible end restrictions. Define A_col,1 as the subspace of actual Coleman functions with analytic differential. Over finite K/ℚ_p construct the K-defined subalgebra and its finite-extension and Galois maps, whose scalar extensions inject into the full ℂ_p algebra. No equality between an algebraic tensor extension and all analytic ℂ_p coefficients is asserted.
hypotheses: U is a Coleman wide open presented on a cofinal strict-neighborhood system; constant field is the geometric coefficient field
For K-valued assertions K/ℚ_p is finite and the branch and data are K-defined
Pullbacks carry compatible Coleman presentations; restrictions preserve a common domain of convergence
prerequisites: roadmap:ColemanIntegration L1.2, L1.17, L1.17a, L1.18–L1.19, L1.43

api.name: fullAnalyticExtension_ker
api.statement: The differential kernel on the full Coleman algebra is the scalar field, so two global primitives differ by one constant.

api.name: fullAnalyticExtension_integrate
api.statement: Every actual Coleman one-form has a global Coleman primitive modulo constants; restrictions of a primitive of an analytic form lie in A_log,1.

api.name: fullAnalyticExtension_map
api.statement: The inclusion from algebraically extended base coefficients is injective and commutes with products, d, primitive classes and end restriction.

tests.name: ColemanWideOpen.fullAnalyticExtension_check1
tests.statement: For U an affine-line wide open and α transcendental over K with |α|<1, (1−αz)⁻¹ on a suitable strict neighborhood is full analytic data but not a finite K-coefficient tensor sum.

tests.name: ColemanWideOpen.fullAnalyticExtension_check2
tests.statement: A scalar has zero differential; log z has differential dz/z and is not scalar. A locally constant indicator on two residue discs is not a Coleman function.

tests.name: ColemanWideOpen.fullAnalyticExtension_check3
tests.statement: Global primitives of R dS and S dR can be shifted to sum to RS. Unrelated constants at different ends need not come from a global primitive.

targets.proofSketch: Extend the existing word/connection realization using full analytic strict-neighborhood sections and their de Rham basis, rather than completing a tensor product by fiat. Reprove faithfulness and the constant kernel on this enlarged coefficient ring by meromorphic pole removal and minimal differential relations. Construct primitive classes in the same unipotent realization. For K-defined data compare local realizations with the supplied algebra by uniqueness. This is the additional full-analytic-coefficient theorem; the base finite/algebraic-coefficient construction is imported.

targets.name: Curve.semistableDeRhamComparison
targets.title: Curve cohomology and the graph maps
targets.statement: For X/K smooth proper geometrically connected with finite reduced boundary Z and a split separated regular nodal realization, using the supplied rigid cohomology, finite-dimensionality, scalar-extension and component dagger comparisons, construct the additional curve algebraic/rigid de Rham comparison with the component-annulus Čech total complex. Its degree-one representatives ((ω_v),(f_e)) satisfy d f_e=ω_tail−ω_head and its coboundaries are ((d a_v),(a_tail−a_head)). Prove the graph exact sequence (4.5), restriction maps, and the graph retraction χ represented by f_e−(F_tail−F_head). Define N_ℓ by the harmonic class of ℓ(e)Res_e(ω_tail) using one fixed rational metric, and identify it with geometric monodromy at that valuation scale. Writing Q_K=#κ_K, construct the K-linear q-Frobenius for q=Q_K^r with integer r≥1 and identity coefficient lift via rigid component cohomology and its weight splitting: χφ=χ, Nφ=qN, χN=N, N²=0. Construct ordered proper cup product and its second-kind local-primitive residue formula. The cohomology, cup, χ and N maps respect coefficient extension and admissible common refinements at one valuation scale; Frobenius extension distinguishes scalar extension of an operator from iteration for the enlarged residue field. For nonsplit Z the scalar-extension maps of complexes are defined before choosing a splitting field.
hypotheses: K/ℚ_p finite, p any prime; X smooth proper geometrically connected of dimension one; a fixed logarithm branch and valuation normalization
Z finite reduced; for displayed split Frobenius charts its points are rational and lie in distinct smooth sections
A split regular nodal model and compatible Coleman cover from §3.0a; common rational metric and fixed valuation scale
Q_K=#κ_K and q=Q_K^r with integer r≥1, so the q-power residue map is the identity; coefficient lift is id_K; the operators are the constructed comparison operators

The supplier linearFrobenius_baseChange law gives F_L=F_K^f⊗1; a scalar-extended operator represents the same q-power geometric Frobenius with identity coefficient lift only if that power fixes κ_L. Residue defines monodromy; the metric convention transports the unit-length formula through §1.3. Compute ordered cup by local second-kind primitives. Prove extension and model maps on these complexes and their agreement on refinements; no index identity or §4.2 is used.

targets.name: ColemanWideOpen.doublePairing
targets.statement: For a connected Coleman wide open U, ω,η analytic one-forms on U and their Coleman primitives F,G, define B_U(ω,η)=Σ_{e∈End(U)} B_e(F|e,G|e), orienting each end by a parameter vanishing in its omitted disc. The value is independent of the two global primitive constants, alternating and agrees under common shrinking of ends. Cohomology factorization, analytic-exact vanishing, rational-core vanishing and logarithmic-unit reciprocity are the subsequent theorems of §3.1a. The same construction allows finitely many punctures by replacing them by sufficiently small omitted discs.

F,G are global Coleman primitives of analytic differentials, with one branch
Use the actual Coleman algebras and end maps of §§3.0a–3.0b
Over K the wide open is geometrically connected with Coleman constant field K; a larger finite constant field is treated over that field and then by trace
The construction is first made after splitting the finite family of ends over the coefficient field; nonsplit ends are traced by §7.5 and descended by §7.6

targets.name: ColemanWideOpen.doublePairing_reciprocity
targets.title: Cohomology and wide-open reciprocity
targets.statement: For a geometrically connected Coleman wide open U with good-reduction compactification C, let B_U be §3.1. Construct the Frobenius-equivariant projection p_U:H¹_dR(U)→H¹_dR(C) splitting proper restriction, and prove B_U(ω,η)=p_U[ω]∪p_U[η]. Hence B_U kills analytic exact forms, factors through H¹_dR(U), vanishes for rational C, and satisfies B_U(F,log f)=0 for every invertible analytic f on U. The supplied component Frobenius spectrum, transported to H¹_dR(U), consists of Weil weight-one eigenvalues and boundary eigenvalues qζ with ζ a root of unity (ζ=1 when the boundary is split); in particular 1/q is absent, the q-eigenspace is in the radical of B_U, and B_U(φ α,φ β)=q B_U(α,β). The assertions hold for full ℂ_p coefficients by comparison, and for K-defined data over finite K.

For Frobenius assertions U descends to finite K/ℚ_p, with a compatible degree-q lift, q=(#κ_K)^r for integer r≥1 and identity coefficient lift; full ℂ_p assertions extend this operator from K
The invertible analytic f and its logarithmic primitive share the given Coleman domain and branch

targets.proofSketch: Use the proper/boundary de Rham sequence and disjoint Frobenius weights to construct p_U. Compute the end-sum by second-kind representatives and prove the compact cup comparison using the local double index, then kill analytic exacts by residue reciprocity. A logarithmic unit has only weight-two boundary class, giving its vanishing. Import the component rigid weight theorem and Gysin sequence, with boundary eigenvalues qζ for nonsplit ends. The cup projection gives the radical and scaling assertions; the positive weights exclude 1/q. This proves the index-dependent claims after the index is defined.

targets.name: Semistable.HarmonicPrimitiveData
targets.statement: For a smooth proper geometrically connected curve X/K with a split regular nodal model and meromorphic ω, remove the poles and choose Coleman primitives F_v on the connected component wide opens. Their differences c_ω(e)=F_head|e−F_tail|e are constants and antisymmetric. Normalize by adding component constants until c_ω is harmonic. At a regular model use unit edge lengths; for subdivisions use the compatible rational metric of §1.3. For a self-node, first take a compatible subdivision giving Coleman component domains; coarsening then adds jumps along its chain, rather than subtracting a primitive from itself. The normalized family exists and is unique up to one common constant, and c_ω is independent of that common constant. The family is a torsor under K, not a distinguished primitive with an invented zero value.
hypotheses: K/ℚ_p finite, p any prime; a fixed branch
X smooth, proper, geometrically connected, dimension one
Chosen split regular nodal realization; pole support separated from the connecting annuli
Component wide opens and their Coleman primitives are those in §§3.0a–3.0b

targets.name: Semistable.correctedDoublePairing

Here χ is the graph retraction constructed in §3.0c, graph representatives of χ are harmonic, and N_ℓ is represented by ℓ(e)Res_e of the differential in a Čech representative. For global meromorphic forms this equals §3.3 with harmonic component jumps. It annihilates algebraic exact forms, restricts to α∪β in that order on proper H¹_dR(X), and is unchanged by refinements between admissible nodal realizations, using the metric when edge lengths change; modifications outside that class are compared after finite extension and regularization. If Z is empty use Čech hypercohomology, rather than pretending all proper classes have global regular representatives.

Z finite reduced and split in this realization; points separated in the model
Use the Čech, cup, χ and monodromy maps constructed in §3.0c
Lengths have one fixed valuation normalization
Every model at which the displayed formula is evaluated is an admissible split nodal realization; a modification outside that class is compared after finite extension and regularization

targets.name: NaturalIntegration.abelianLogCp
targets.title: Abelian logarithms for arbitrary geometric coefficients
targets.statement: For every abelian variety A defined over ℂ_p, construct the unique locally ℂ_p-analytic additive homomorphism log_A:A(ℂ_p)→Lie(A)(ℂ_p) whose differential at the identity is the identity. No model over a finite extension of ℚ_p is required. It is independent of the scalar logarithm branch. This extends the class of varieties covered by the logarithm supplier over finite extensions of ℚ_p; for varieties descending to a finite p-adic field, identify the result with the supplied construction.

A an abelian variety over ℂ_p of any dimension and arbitrary reduction

api.statement: Every locally ℂ_p-analytic additive homomorphism A(ℂ_p)→Lie(A)(ℂ_p) with identity differential equals log_A. In particular log_A is zero on torsion points and restricts to an analytic group isomorphism on a sufficiently small open subgroup.

It has no finite p-adic field model, but log_{E_t} and invariant-form primitives are covered here, including p=2 and 3. Extending points of a variety defined over a finite p-adic field does not cover this example.

targets.proofSketch: Construct the normalized local analytic logarithm by integrating invariant forms near the identity; its differential is the identity, so it is an analytic group isomorphism after shrinking. Prove the open-quotient torsion theorem for arbitrary A/ℂ_p using the geometric deformation argument of Theorem II.1.9, including varieties without a finite p-adic field model. No compactness of A(ℂ_p) is assumed. For x choose n≥1 with [n]x in the local subgroup and set log_A(x)=n⁻¹ log_V([n]x). Local additivity and common multiples prove independence and additivity. Translation proves local analyticity. A competing homomorphism with the same differential agrees locally, and torsion of the quotient forces global agreement in the characteristic-zero Lie algebra. Apply the same argument to invariant-form evaluations to prove homomorphism compatibility. The transported finite-model logarithm has the required differential and analyticity, so uniqueness gives the comparison on all ℂ_p-points.

targets.name: NaturalIntegration.abelianPrimitive
targets.title: Natural primitives on abelian varieties
targets.statement: For an abelian variety A over a finite p-adic field or ℂ_p and every closed rational one-form ω, construct a locally log-meromorphic primitive F_ω modulo one affine scalar constant. Let Δ_h F(x)=F(x+h)−F(x). Over ℂ_p the algebraic theorem of the square makes Δ_hΔ_kω exact in rational functions and scalar logarithms; normalize its primitive to vanish when h=k=0. Over a finite p-adic field use the descended span of traces Tr_{L/K}(c dlog f), with L/K finite separable, c∈L and f∈L(A³)×, together with rational exact forms; its primitive uses Tr_{L/K}(c log_univ f). Require Δ_hΔ_k F_ω to be that primitive. Prove existence, uniqueness, linearity, compatibility with homomorphisms and evaluation of rational exact and logarithmic forms. Prove the finite-difference splitting theorem for symmetric locally log-meromorphic additive cocycles needed for this construction. On invariant holomorphic forms over finite K use the supplied abelian logarithm; for arbitrary A/ℂ_p use §4.0 and its finite-model comparison.
hypotheses: p any prime; K/ℚ_p finite, or coefficients in ℂ_p with the same universal logarithm
A is an abelian variety; ω closed rational; all evaluations avoid its poles
Universal values lie in K+K T (respectively ℂ_p+ℂ_p T), with log_univ(p)=T

Prove the finite K/ℚ_p version on A(K) for K+K T-valued cocycles, with traced scalar logarithms, and compatibility of the normalized differential rigidification with extension to ℂ_p.

api.name: abelianPrimitive_square
api.statement: Over ℂ_p construct the normalized rational-logarithmic primitive of the second difference of every closed rational ω. api.name: abelianPrimitive_descent

Continuous Galois conjugation acts coefficientwise with T fixed. For every finite L/K the same difference on embedded endpoints is its coefficientwise image; these comparisons compose in towers.

tests.name: NaturalIntegration.abelianPrimitive_check2
tests.statement: An invariant form has second difference zero and its based primitive is the abelian logarithm pairing. An unrelated locally constant function with zero derivative need not obey the finite-difference condition.

tests.name: NaturalIntegration.abelianPrimitive_check3
tests.statement: For a rational function f, F_df=f modulo constants; the zero form has only scalar constant ambiguity, not arbitrary residue-disc constants.

tests.name: NaturalIntegration.abelianPrimitive_descent
tests.statement: For a K-defined rational f on A, the normalized primitive of df is f−f(a) and is fixed by G_K. Enlarging K to L does not multiply it by [L:K]; an averaged trace, rather than an unnormalized trace of the whole primitive, is needed for descent.

targets.proofSketch: Establish the algebraic square identity and its normalized rational-logarithmic primitive geometrically; for K-defined data descend this finite algebraic expression by normalized trace, including traced scalar logarithms. Prove symmetric cocycle splitting by convergent local analytic differences and division in the coefficient field. Over finite K, apply it to this K-valued cocycle on A(K), obtaining a K+K T-valued primitive; completeness keeps the convergent coefficients in K. Subtract the K-defined invariant differential error with the imported abelian logarithm. Over arbitrary A/ℂ_p subtract that error using abelianLogCp of §4.0; its finite-model comparison identifies the two corrections whenever A descends. Run the construction over each finite L/K and over ℂ_p. The common square identity and differential rigidification identify restrictions modulo constants: their difference has zero differential and zero second difference. Its apparent singularities cancel, leaving a locally constant additive map modulo a scalar; properness makes A(K) compact, so this map has finite image and vanishes in the characteristic-zero target. Normalization at a regular K-point identifies the based values. Conjugating the construction transports every coefficient and logarithm, so uniqueness gives Galois equivariance with T fixed. Thus rationality and finite-extension independence precede natural integration, using the finite-field construction rather than an additional completed-field fixed-point theorem. The same uniqueness proves linearity, exact evaluation and algebraic pullback without a semistable graph.

targets.name: NaturalIntegration.albaneseReduction
targets.title: Reduction of closed rational forms to the Albanese
targets.statement: For a smooth geometrically connected variety X over a characteristic-zero field k with a chosen rational point, construct its proper Albanese on the native IsAlbanese predicate via a smooth projective compactification of a dense quasi-projective open and extension of rational maps to abelian varieties. Over algebraically closed k, pullback is an isomorphism on closed rational one-forms modulo the k-span of df and dlog f, giving ω=a_X*η+df₀+Σ_i c_i dlog f_i. Over arbitrary k, define `NaturalIntegration.descendedLogForms`, denoted LogDesc_k(X), as the k-span of Tr_{L(X)/k(X)}(c dlog f), for finite separable L/k, c∈L and f∈L(X)×; the differential trace is the coefficient trace under Ω¹_{L(X)/L}≃L⊗_k Ω¹_{k(X)/k}. Pullback gives the corresponding quotient isomorphism modulo d(k(X))+LogDesc_k(X). Thus over k the decomposition uses a finite sum of these traced logarithmic terms. For k-defined data choose the geometric decomposition over an algebraic closure k̄/k, then embed k̄ into any desired algebraically closed overfield E. Full logarithmic spanning holds over k̄; over arbitrary E it identifies only the span generated by rational functions defined over finite algebraic extensions of k inside E. Genuinely E-defined data use the geometric rational-form comparison over E itself. Prove functoriality, compatibility with finite separable extension, and moving of apparent poles away from finite regular evaluation sets. Over finite p-adic k, pull back the abelian primitive and add f₀ and the traced scalar universal logarithms. Its based value is k-rational, independent of the decomposition and finite field of definition, and extends where ω is regular. This comparison concerns rational forms and the proper Albanese.
hypotheses: k a characteristic-zero field; algebraic closedness only for the untraced geometric decomposition; finite p-adic k or ℂ_p for primitive assertions
X smooth geometrically connected finite type with a rational point a, and ω closed rational
Evaluation points are outside the poles of ω; auxiliary decompositions may have additional poles; traces use finite separable constant extensions

api.name: albaneseReduction_rationalForms
api.statement: Over algebraically closed k pullback identifies closed rational forms modulo d(k(X))+span_k{dlog f}. Over arbitrary characteristic-zero k it identifies the quotients modulo rational exact forms and LogDesc_k on X and its Albanese. These quotient comparisons commute with finite separable coefficient extension.

api.name: albaneseReduction_removeApparentPoles
api.statement: For k-defined data and any finite set of regular algebraic points, including the base point, choose the geometric decomposition over k̄/k with no apparent poles there, descend after a common finite extension of k, and only then embed into E or ℂ_p. For data defined over E itself, use the independent geometric decomposition over E; primitive assertions retain the finite p-adic or ℂ_p coefficient hypotheses. Its based primitive extends to the regular locus and is independent of that choice.

api.name: albaneseReduction_functorial
api.statement: An algebraic morphism induces the pointed Albanese comparison. On a dense open where the chosen rational expressions pull back, it respects rational exact forms and LogDesc_k; moving gives the based primitive pullback wherever the original form is regular.

api.name: albaneseReduction_primitiveDescent
api.statement: For finite K/ℚ_p, a K-defined X,ω and regular a,b∈X(K), the based geometric primitive constructed from §4.0a, rational functions and scalar logarithms belongs to K+K T by the finite-field construction and traced logarithms; its geometric comparison is fixed by G_K with T fixed. Every finite L/K gives the coefficientwise embedded value, independent of splitting field, apparent-pole removal and decomposition; these identifications compose in towers. The assertion follows from abelianPrimitive_descent and geometric decomposition independence, without §7.3 or naturalIntegration.

api.name: descendedLogForms_add
api.statement: For characteristic-zero k and X as above, LogDesc_k(X) is closed under addition: concatenate finite traced logarithmic presentations.

api.name: descendedLogForms_smul
api.statement: For a∈k, scaling a traced generator gives Tr_{L(X)/k(X)}((ac)dlog f); in particular zero belongs to LogDesc_k(X).

api.name: descendedLogForms_split
api.statement: In every algebraically closed overfield E/k, each traced generator becomes Σ_σ σ(c)dlog(σf), over k-embeddings σ:L→E. For an algebraic closure k̄/k, the k̄-span of the scalar-extended LogDesc_k(X) is the full logarithmic subspace span_{k̄}{dlog f : f∈k̄(X)×}. For arbitrary algebraically closed E/k its E-span equals only span_E{dlog f : f∈L(X)×, k⊆L⊆E finite algebraic}; no equality with all E-rational logarithmic forms is asserted.

api.name: descendedLogForms_tower
api.statement: For finite separable M/L/k, iterated differential traces agree with direct trace. Presentations computed in a larger normal closure therefore define the same k-subspace; averaging uses the reciprocal of the extension degree.

tests.name: NaturalIntegration.albaneseReduction_check1
tests.statement: For A¹ with ω=dt use f₀=t and no Albanese contribution; its proper Albanese is zero.

tests.name: NaturalIntegration.albaneseReduction_check2

tests.name: NaturalIntegration.albaneseReduction_check3

tests.name: NaturalIntegration.albaneseReduction_quadraticPole
tests.statement: Over k=ℚ₃ take X=ℙ¹, α²=2 and ω=dt/(t²−2). Its residues ±1/(2α) are not in k, so no k-linear sum of dlog of k-rational functions, even with an exact term, represents it. Instead ω=Tr_{k(α)/k}((1/(2α))dlog(t−α)); its based primitive is the trace of (1/(2α))log_univ((t−α)/(a−α)), and further finite extension leaves this value unchanged.

tests.name: NaturalIntegration.albaneseReduction_normalizedTrace
tests.statement: For ω=dt defined over k, averaging an expression over a quadratic extension gives (1/2)Tr(dt)=dt; using Tr without the factor 1/2 gives 2dt. For a point the quotient and based primitive are zero, over every constant extension.

tests.name: NaturalIntegration.descendedLogForms_nonexample
tests.statement: On ℙ¹, dt has a double pole at infinity and is not in LogDesc_k(ℙ¹): every traced scalar logarithmic derivative has at most simple poles. In contrast dt/t is logarithmic, and the nonsplit quadratic form above belongs through its trace. Exact forms and descended logarithmic forms are distinct subspaces.

tests.name: NaturalIntegration.descendedLogForms_transcendentalPole
tests.statement: For k=ℚ, E=ℂ, X=ℙ¹ and α transcendental over ℚ, dt/(t−α)=dlog(t−α) is logarithmic over E with residue 1 at α. Every finite E-linear combination of scalar-extended traced generators from finite algebraic extensions of ℚ is regular at α, so the E-span is strictly smaller than the full E-logarithmic subspace. The geometric rational-form decomposition over E still includes this form.

targets.proofSketch: Use the supplied compactification on a dense quasi-projective open, construct the proper Albanese on its native universal property and extend its rational map across the smooth variety. Prove the rational residue/Picard comparison over any algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, giving its geometric quotient isomorphism. For X,ω defined over k, first choose this decomposition over an algebraic closure k̄/k. Its finitely many coefficients then lie in a finite algebraic extension of k. In a finite Galois extension containing that field, average conjugates: η and f₀ descend by normalized trace, and each logarithmic term becomes a trace of c dlog f divided by the extension degree. Conversely each trace splits into scalar logarithmic derivatives. For any f over a finite separable L/k, write L=k(θ). The matrix (σ(θ)^j) for 0≤j<[L:k] is a Vandermonde matrix with nonzero determinant, since the embeddings σ have distinct values on θ. Inverting the trace identities Tr(θ^j dlog f)=Σ_σ σ(θ)^j dlog(σf) expresses every conjugate dlog f as a k̄-linear combination of traces. This proves full spanning over k̄ and, after embedding k̄ in E, exactly the finite-algebraic-field-of-definition span over E. It gives no spanning statement for rational functions with transcendental coefficients. The same averaging proves quotient injectivity. Division is legitimate in characteristic zero, and a non-Galois extension is handled in a normal closure by trace transitivity. This also proves coefficient-extension compatibility of the descended quotient. For genuinely E-defined data use the geometric rational-form comparison over E itself; when E=ℂ_p, prove geometric primitive independence using the rational-logarithmic constant kernel and §4.0a. For k-defined data perform the decomposition and apparent-pole removal over k̄ before embedding into E or ℂ_p. Galois conjugation then preserves the based primitive; abelianPrimitive_descent and coefficientwise traced logarithms give rationality and finite-extension independence before §4.0c. Curve Albanese is the supplied pointed Jacobian.

targets.name: SingleIntegral.naturalIntegration
targets.title: The all-prime natural single integral
targets.statement: For every prime p, every finite K/ℚ_p, every smooth geometrically connected finite-type variety U/K, closed regular one-form ω and a,b∈U(K), construct the unique natural single-integration theory with universal value A+B T in K[T]. It is K-linear in ω, locally analytic in endpoints, differentiates to ω in the second endpoint, vanishes at a=b and satisfies Chasles. It commutes with algebraic pullback, integrates df and dlog f by endpoint differences and the universal logarithm, agrees with the supplied Coleman single integral under good reduction, and respects finite scalar extension and Galois conjugation with T fixed. Apply this to complements of poles of any meromorphic curve form. No graph, genus or reduction condition enters existence or uniqueness. Uniqueness concerns the whole natural theory across varieties. Vologodsky2001 Proposition 52, §17.2, p. 42, line 1806 identifies this with that preprint’s single integral under its p>2 standing convention (line 51); the all-prime theorem uses Colmez.
hypotheses: p any prime, including 2 and 3; K/ℚ_p finite
U smooth geometrically connected finite type; ω regular and closed; endpoints K-rational and off all excluded poles
For extended endpoints and forms use the specified finite scalar extension; the branch λ lies in K

locator.where: Definitions II.1.2–II.1.3 and Theorem II.1.4, pp. 73–74, colmez1998 lines 2982–2997; proof pp. 83–85, lines 3395–3431; Remark 2, pp. 2–3, lines 229–258

api.name: singleIntegral_universalAffine
api.statement: The natural integral belongs to the affine subspace K+K T; evaluate T=λ for the chosen branch.

api.name: singleIntegral_baseChange
api.statement: For finite L/K the pullback form and embedded endpoints have the coefficientwise embedded universal integral; the maps compose in towers.

api.name: singleIntegral_goodReduction
api.statement: For a good-reduction Coleman presentation and a fixed branch, natural and supplied Coleman integration agree.

api.name: singleIntegral_exact_log

tests.name: SingleIntegral.naturalIntegration_check2

tests.name: SingleIntegral.naturalIntegration_check3

targets.proofSketch: Apply the geometric reduction and descended logarithmic quotient of §4.0b with the rigidified abelian primitives of §4.0a, subtract endpoint values, and use moving to remove artificial poles. The named albaneseReduction_primitiveDescent supplies K-rationality and finite-extension independence before this construction. Decomposition independence gives linearity and naturality; endpoint differences give Chasles. The construction is affine in the universal logarithm. Compare the same auxiliary varieties and primitives in good reduction with the supplied Coleman theory. The coefficient and Galois maps are those already proved in §§4.0a–4.0b; natural-theory uniqueness identifies their induced integration laws, without using the later §7.3. This is not uniqueness from derivatives alone.

targets.name: Curve.naturalIndexReciprocity
targets.title: Natural principal-divisor reciprocity
targets.statement: For X/K smooth proper geometrically connected, a meromorphic ω, its natural primitive F from §4.0c and f∈K(X)× with divisor disjoint from the poles of ω, prove Σ_x B_x(F,log f)=0, summing over the singularities of the two primitives after splitting. Local germs are taken in smooth point parameters, not on entire component wide opens. Consequently the natural integral on (f) equals Σ_{x at a pole of ω} Res_x(log f·ω), with log f analytic near those poles. The result uses no harmonic realization theorem.
hypotheses: p any prime; finite K/ℚ_p; X smooth proper geometrically connected
ω meromorphic; f nonzero rational and div(f) disjoint from poles of ω
First take a finite extension splitting the finite supports; local logarithm branches and F are compatible

locator.where: arXiv math/0301029v1, Proposition 3.4 and Lemmas 3.5–3.7, pp. 8–9, besser2005 lines 355–380; application in besser-zerbes2017 §2, p. 4, lines 151–167; natural integration from colmez1998 Theorem II.1.4

api.name: naturalIndexReciprocity_principal
api.statement: The principal-divisor natural integral equals the residue expression, with F in the first local-index slot.

api.name: naturalIndexReciprocity_constants
api.statement: Changing F by a global scalar changes the total by that scalar times the degree of div(f), hence zero.

api.name: naturalIndexReciprocity_finiteDegree
api.statement: For a finite surjective morphism h:X→Y of smooth proper geometrically connected curves over a finite p-adic field or ℂ_p, with one branch and meromorphic α,β on Y, define B_X^nat(α,β) as the sum of local indices of their natural primitives after splitting singularities. Then B_X^nat(h*α,h*β)=deg(h) B_Y^nat(α,β), with local ramification multiplicities included (besser2005 Lemma 3.6, line 365).

api.name: naturalIndexReciprocity_projection
api.statement: For the same h, meromorphic α on Y and β on X, the separable differential trace satisfies B_X^nat(h*α,β)=B_Y^nat(α,Tr_h β). Define Tr_h on rational differential germs through the finite separable function-field trace. In a Galois closure, h*Tr_h β is the sum of conjugate pullbacks; natural primitive sums have the same differential and rigidification modulo constants (besser2005 Lemma 3.7, line 369).

api.name: naturalIndexReciprocity_rationalLine
api.statement: On ℙ¹ over an algebraically closed p-adic coefficient field, B^nat(dlog t,dlog(t−a))=0 for every a, and B^nat(dg,dlog t)=0 for rational g. The first is a direct computation at 0,a,∞, with a=0 handled by alternation; the second is the proper residue theorem (besser2005 Lemma 3.5, line 358, and Proposition 3.4 proof, line 376).

tests.name: Curve.naturalIndexReciprocity_check2

targets.proofSketch: First define the global natural double-index sum using §4.0c and prove finite-map degree scaling from the local ramification law of §2.3. Define the differential trace for the finite separable function-field extension. In a Galois closure, naturality makes the primitive of the trace the sum of conjugate primitives modulo a scalar; global residue cancellation removes that scalar. Divide the degree formula by the nonzero covering degree to obtain the projection formula. For nonconstant f the induced map X→ℙ¹ is finite and projection reduces B_X^nat(ω,dlog f) to B_ℙ¹^nat(Tr_f ω,dlog t). Over the algebraically closed coefficient field, partial fractions split Tr_f ω into an exact rational differential and scalar logarithmic derivatives. Compute the logarithmic pair at 0,a,∞; the exact term vanishes by the residue theorem. Descend by the early primitive compatibility in §4.0b; constant f is handled separately. Finally, at div(f) the local term is ord_x(f)F(x), while at poles of ω it is −Res_x(log f·ω). This yields the separated-support formula before harmonic realization.

targets.name: Curve.jacobianIntegrationBridge
targets.title: Jacobian differentials and point topology
targets.statement: For X/K smooth proper geometrically connected with a chosen b∈X(K), identify holomorphic curve forms with pullbacks of invariant differentials on J=Jac(X) and prove I_univ(a,c;ω)=ω_J(abelianLog([c−a])). Prove J(K) is compact. The subgroup H generated by differences of K-rational points is open and compact: the differential of an Abel–Jacobi sum X^g→J is surjective at a suitable tuple of K-points. An additive locally constant map H→K is therefore zero. Prove moving of divisors away from a fixed finite pole set for the divisor-class argument. When X has no K-point, apply these assertions after a finite extension containing a temporary point; do not manufacture an unpointed Abel–Jacobi morphism.
hypotheses: K/ℚ_p finite, p any prime; X smooth proper geometrically connected
A temporary K-rational base point for the pointed assertions; holomorphic ω for the logarithm identity
The vanishing assertion requires an additive locally constant map on the compact subgroup H, not on an arbitrary noncompact group

locator.where: Lemma II.1.13 and Remark II.1.18, pp. 78–79, colmez1998 lines 3147–3159 and 3213–3214; besser-zerbes2017 §2, pp. 3–4, lines 142–150

api.name: jacobianIntegrationBridge_natural
api.statement: Natural integration of holomorphic forms is evaluation of the supplied abelian logarithm on the degree-zero Abel–Jacobi class.

api.name: jacobianIntegrationBridge_compact

api.name: jacobianIntegrationBridge_moving
api.statement: Divisor representatives can be moved away from the pole set; local sections of Abel–Jacobi sums make a divisor functional with zero derivative locally constant on H.

tests.name: Curve.jacobianIntegrationBridge_check2

targets.proofSketch: Use the supplied Abel–Jacobi differential identification and §4.0c naturality, comparing invariant forms with §4.0a and the supplied abelian logarithm. Properness over a locally compact field gives compact rational points. Nonzero holomorphic forms cannot vanish at every point of a residue disc, so choose g evaluation points giving an invertible differential matrix; the analytic inverse theorem makes H open. A locally constant homomorphism from compact H has finite image, which is zero in characteristic zero. Moving and these local sections supply the divisor-topology bridge used in §4.2.

targets.name: Semistable.dlog_residue_is_exact
targets.statement: In a split regular semistable model, if f is a nonzero rational function whose divisor has support away from all connecting annuli, then Res_e(dlog f)=ord_head(f)−ord_tail(f)=−d(ord)(e), where ord_v is the multiplicity of the vertical component in div(f). Thus the residue cochain of dlog f is exact. The functions f and log_λ f are global component primitives of df and dlog f respectively, so both have zero harmonic jumps wherever defined.

f≠0 and has neither zero nor pole on a connecting annulus
At a node xy=π, tail=(y), head=(x), Res_e(dx/x)=1

This comparison holds for every prime and every genus. Loops and parallel edges are retained through their flags or a compatible subdivision.

ω meromorphic; every evaluated point lies outside its poles
A split regular semistable realization with separated supports is chosen for the comparison

targets.proofSketch: For principal D=(f), compare the natural reciprocity of §4.0d with §3.3 for the harmonic family; no Coleman restriction of the natural primitive is assumed. §3.1a kills the component pairings, and §4.1 with harmonic-exact orthogonality kills the correction. The moving and local-section theorem of §4.0e makes it locally constant on H; compactness of H gives finite image, hence zero in the torsion-free additive field. This proves smooth-residue comparison. Annular values are proved separately in §4.3.

targets.name: Annulus.TripleIndexData
targets.statement: For three labelled functions F,G,H in A_log,1, define TripleIndexData to consist of primitives I_{R dS} in A_log for every labelled pair, with dI_{R dS}=R dS and I_{R dS}+I_{S dR}=RS. On the diagonal set I_{R dR}=R²/2. Distinct labels retain their choices even when their functions happen to coincide. Such data exist. Choices for each unordered off-diagonal pair form a torsor under k, acting by I_{R dS}↦I_{R dS}+C and I_{S dR}↦I_{S dR}−C. Data may be permuted, pulled back and combined linearly with their functions; no arbitrary primitive choices are silently identified.
hypotheses: Characteristic-zero field k and the formal ring of §2.1; or its analytic open-annulus version
All differential and product equations are imposed on the actual functions
In the analytic case all functions and primitives share a domain of convergence

locator.where: §7, equation (7.2) and the data before Proposition 7.3, pp. 355–356, besser-dejeu2012 line 2232 and line 2251

api.name: TripleIndexData.mk
api.statement: Choose a primitive for one direction of each unordered pair and set the reverse to RS−I; use R²/2 on the diagonal.

api.name: TripleIndexData.ext
api.statement: Equality is equality of the three functions and their labelled primitive entries.

api.name: TripleIndexData.changeConstant
api.statement: The indicated opposite shifts preserve all derivative and integration-by-parts equations; any two choices are related by unique pair constants.

api.name: TripleIndexData.pullback
api.statement: Differential-compatible annular or formal substitutions pull back every entry, preserving products and pair equations.

api.name: TripleIndexData.linearCombination
api.statement: Mixed-pair auxiliary primitives for a linear combination are the same linear combination of the original mixed entries; reverse entries satisfy integration by parts, and a new diagonal entry is recomputed as R²/2.

tests.name: Annulus.TripleIndexData_1

tests.name: Annulus.TripleIndexData_2

tests.name: Annulus.TripleIndexData_3

Only the formal case uses the integration-by-parts induction in k((z))[L], dividing by n+1 or j+1 as appropriate. Choose one entry per unordered labelled pair and define the reverse as RS−I; set the diagonal to R²/2. The constant kernel gives the torsor law. These are new compatible choice data, not another construction of the analytic primitive theorem.
targets.title: Compatible labelled auxiliary primitives

targets.name: Annulus.tripleIndex
targets.statement: For compatible TripleIndexData define T_e(F,G;H) as the unique scalar operation that is trilinear under the compatible linear combinations of §5.1, symmetric in F,G, satisfies T(F,G;H)+T(F,H;G)+T(G,H;F)=0 with the same permuted auxiliary entries, and equals B_e(F,I_{G dH}) when G has no logarithmic term. Existence and uniqueness hold in the formal and analytic annular settings. T is an operation on the full auxiliary data, not a trilinear map on three bare functions.
hypotheses: Hypotheses and actual primitive equations of §5.1
The analytic-first reduction uses Res(dG)=0

locator.where: Proposition 7.3, Lemma 7.5 and equation (7.6), pp. 356–359, besser-dejeu2012 line 2277 and line 2327

api.name: tripleIndex_unique
api.statement: Any scalar operation on the same data satisfying the four stated laws equals T.

api.name: tripleIndex_symm
api.statement: T(F,G;H)=T(G,F;H) with the natural permutation of primitive entries.

api.name: tripleIndex_threeTerm
api.statement: The three cyclic placements of the distinguished third slot sum to zero with common auxiliary data.

api.name: tripleIndex_meromorphic
api.statement: If F,G have no logarithmic term then T(F,G;H)=Res_e(FG dH).

tests.name: Annulus.tripleIndex_1
tests.statement: T(1,1;L)=1 and T(z,z;z⁻²)=−2 by the Laurent-first rule. These computed values detect the order of the differentiated third slot; the three-term identity uses one common labelled primitive data set.

tests.name: Annulus.tripleIndex_2
tests.statement: With F=G=H=L and all I=L²/2, T=0, since three equal summands give 3T=0. This holds over ℚ₃ because 3 is nonzero.

tests.name: Annulus.tripleIndex_3
tests.statement: For Laurent F=z,G=z⁻¹,H=L, T=Res(dz/z)=1; an index that always vanishes on rational-function slots fails.

targets.proofSketch: Expand each function into Laurent part plus scalar L. If one slot is Laurent, the reduction, symmetry and three-term identity determine the value; integration by parts proves consistency on intersections of those cases. For three L slots choose all half squares, making the value zero. Extend by compatible trilinearity and derive the conditional choice-change formulas from these axioms and use them to compare arbitrary primitive choices; §5.3 exports those formulas after existence.
targets.title: Existence and characterization of the local index

targets.name: Annulus.tripleIndex_changeConstant
targets.statement: Increasing I_{G dH} by C and decreasing I_{H dG} by C changes T(F,G;H) by −C Res_e(dF). Changing the F,H pair similarly changes it by −C Res_e(dG). It is independent of the F,G pair. Simultaneous pair changes add these effects. In particular zero in a function slot does not force the local value to vanish when its associated auxiliary data are not the compatible zero data.
hypotheses: TripleIndexData as in §5.1
C∈k; the opposite primitive is shifted by −C
Functions and all other primitive entries are fixed

locator.where: Lemma 7.4, p. 357, besser-dejeu2012 line 2299

api.name: tripleIndex_changeBoth
api.statement: Changing the G,H pair by C and the F,H pair by D changes the value by −C Res(dF)−D Res(dG).

tests.name: Annulus.tripleIndex_changeConstant_1

tests.name: Annulus.tripleIndex_changeConstant_2

tests.name: Annulus.tripleIndex_changeConstant_3

targets.proofSketch: Use the reduction rule on the added data (F,0;H), where I_{0 dH}=C. Then T(F,0;H)=B(F,C)=−C Res(dF). Symmetry gives the other law, and changing the unused F,G pair has no effect in the generating cases, hence in general.

targets.name: Annulus.tripleIndex_simplePoles
targets.statement: In the formal case assume dF,dG,dH have at most simple poles at z=0. Write c_z for the constant coefficient of the L⁰ Laurent coefficient in A_log. Then T(F,G;H)=c_z(F)c_z(G)Res(dH)−Res(dF)c_z(I_{G dH})−Res(dG)c_z(I_{F dH}). The coefficient c_z is parameter dependent; the whole expression, with all functions and primitive data transported, is parameter independent.

TripleIndexData of §5.1
dF,dG,dH have no poles of order greater than one at the formal origin

tests.name: Annulus.tripleIndex_simplePoles_2

tests.name: Annulus.tripleIndex_simplePoles_3

targets.name: Annulus.tripleIndex_pullback
targets.statement: Orientation reversal negates the triple index with fixed functions and auxiliary data. For an orientation-preserving finite map φ:e′→e of annuli of degree n≥1, or a formal substitution of positive order n, T_e′(φ*F,φ*G;φ*H)=n T_e(F,G;H), provided every auxiliary primitive is pulled back. In particular parameter isomorphisms preserve T. Restrictions of ends and scalar embeddings also preserve the index on transported data.

φ finite with positive degree and compatible orientations
All functions, branches and primitive entries are transported together

locator.where: §8 parameter independence and Lemma 8.1, p. 361, besser-dejeu2012 line 2524; orientation/scalar consequences of the characterization

api.statement: Degrees multiply under composable pullbacks and scalar embeddings commute with the degree law.

tests.statement: z=t² sends (1,1;log z) with its primitives to (1,1;2log t), and T changes from 1 to 2.

tests.name: Annulus.tripleIndex_pullback_2

tests.name: Annulus.tripleIndex_pullback_3

The residue degree law of §2.3 and uniqueness of §5.2 recover the original index; reversal and scalar extension use the same characterization. Restricting Laurent expansions to a common annulus preserves every term.
targets.title: Orientation, parameter and degree laws

targets.name: ColemanWideOpen.formSymbolRelations
targets.title: Relations among actual Coleman forms
targets.statement: Let A_col,1(U) be the actual Coleman functions with analytic differential in §3.0b, and let Ω¹_col,1(U) be the submodule of actual Coleman forms generated by Gη with G∈A_col,1(U), η analytic. Construct the well-defined symbol map Ω¹_col,1(U)→H¹_dR(U)⊗Ω¹(U), Gη↦[dG]⊗η. For the product presentation m:A_col,1(U)⊗Ω¹(U)→Ω¹_col,1(U), prove ker(m) is contained in the image of A(U)⊗Ω¹(U). Thus equal actual forms have equal symbols. This is a theorem about the actual connection/word realization, not a defining relation imposed on a free module.
hypotheses: U geometrically connected Coleman wide open with finite ends; coefficients ℂ_p or K-defined data as in §3.0b
All tensors are over the coefficient field; η is analytic
The function/form products and equalities are those of the constructed full Coleman algebra

targets.name: ColemanWideOpen.tripleIndex

Restrictions of these global choices, rather than unrelated local choices at each end, are part of the construction. Over a finite extension K/ℚ_p use functions and auxiliary data defined over K or scalar extension with descent as in §7.6; over ℂ_p take the same end-sum.

F,G,H global Coleman functions with dF,dG,dH analytic on U
A common branch and global compatible Coleman auxiliary primitives
Over K the wide open is geometrically connected with Coleman constant field K; a larger finite constant field is treated over that field and then by trace
The construction is first made after splitting the finite family of ends over the coefficient field; nonsplit ends are traced by §7.5 and descended by §7.6

api.name: tripleIndex_congr

tests.name: ColemanWideOpen.tripleIndex_2

targets.title: The global end-sum

targets.name: ColemanWideOpen.tripleIndex_laws
targets.statement: The end-sum of §6.1 is independent of the global auxiliary primitives, is k-trilinear in the actual functions, is symmetric in the first two slots and satisfies the three-term identity. For a scalar C, T_U(F,C;H)=C B_U(F,H) and T_U(F,G;C)=0. Hence replacing G by G+C changes the value by C B_U(F,H). It is preserved on common smaller end annuli and on deleting discs across which all three functions and their global auxiliary data extend as Coleman data with analytic differentials. A restriction theorem carries that extension hypothesis; it does not allow arbitrary singular excisions.
hypotheses: Hypotheses of §6.1
Auxiliary changes are global constants on connected U
Shrinking preserves the core, or has the stated extension across added discs

locator.where: Lemmas 8.2–8.3, pp. 361–362, besser-dejeu2012 line 2546; introduction p. 310, line 250, for shrinking

api.name: tripleIndex_add_const_second
api.statement: T_U(F,G+C;H)−T_U(F,G;H)=C B_U(F,H).

api.name: tripleIndex_const_third
api.statement: T_U(F,G;C)=0 for any constant C.

api.name: tripleIndex_restrict
api.statement: Compatible repeated shrinking gives the same value, including any finite chain of common end restrictions.

tests.name: ColemanWideOpen.tripleIndex_laws_1
tests.statement: For B_U(F,H)=1, adding 2 to G adds 2 to T_U; it is not a pairing of three differential classes.

tests.name: ColemanWideOpen.tripleIndex_laws_2
tests.statement: A global shift C in I_{G dH} changes the sum by −CΣ_e Res_e(dF)=0, even if individual residues are nonzero.

tests.name: ColemanWideOpen.tripleIndex_laws_3
tests.statement: On an annular rational wide open with end residues +1 and −1, changing the auxiliary primitive only at the first end by 1 changes the sum by −1. Local choices do not cancel without global compatibility.

targets.proofSketch: Sum §5.3 and use the residue theorem for the analytic one-form dF. This gives auxiliary independence and ordinary trilinearity. Reduction with G=C gives C B_U(F,H); the three-term identity and alternation of B_U give zero in the third slot. Restriction uses §5.5; an added filled disc has total zero index from analytic local primitives and the residue theorem.
targets.title: Choice cancellation, constants and shrinking

targets.name: ColemanWideOpen.tripleIndex_frobenius_vanishing
targets.statement: Let U be a Coleman wide open defined over a finite K/ℚ_p with a degree-q Frobenius lift in the supplied rigid-cohomology sense, q=(#κ_K)^r for integer r≥1 and identity coefficient lift. If φ*[dF]=q[dF] and φ*[dG]=q[dG] in H¹_dR(U), then T_U(F,G;H)=0 for every global Coleman H with analytic differential. The assertion also includes zero classes. It uses the supplied spectrum theorem excluding 1/q from Frobenius on H¹_dR(U), and the fact that the q-eigenspace is in the radical of B_U.
hypotheses: Hypotheses of §6.1; U and data descend to a finite p-adic field
A compatible degree-q Frobenius lift with q=(#κ_K)^r, integer r≥1 and identity coefficient lift, as in §3.0c
Both stated q-eigenclass equations
§3.1a supplies the spectrum and double-pairing radical properties

locator.where: Proposition 8.4 and proof, p. 362, besser-dejeu2012 line 2591

api.name: tripleIndex_frobenius_iterate
api.statement: For a≥1, use φ^a, degree q^a=(#κ_K)^{ra} and both corresponding q^a-eigenclass hypotheses. Under finite L/K of residue degree f the geometric operator is φ^f⊗1 with degree q^f, using §3.0c; q-eigenclasses extend to q^f-eigenclasses for it. A mere scalar extension of φ is not automatically that geometric operator.

tests.name: ColemanWideOpen.tripleIndex_frobenius_vanishing_1
tests.statement: F=0 satisfies the eigenclass condition and gives zero; p=2 and q=2 are admitted over ℚ₂. Over its unramified quadratic extension the identity-coefficient lift instead uses q=4; q=2 fails the residue condition.

tests.name: ColemanWideOpen.tripleIndex_frobenius_vanishing_2
tests.statement: A general F with B_U(F,H)=1 and G=1 gives T_U=1. The theorem cannot drop the q-eigenclass hypothesis on F.

tests.name: ColemanWideOpen.tripleIndex_frobenius_vanishing_3
tests.statement: The proof produces L(φ*γ)=q⁻¹L(γ). At q=2 this is eigenvalue 1/2, not 2 or 1; the excluded reciprocal is essential.

targets.proofSketch: Write φ*F=qF+r and φ*G=qG+s with analytic r,s, absorbing global constants into r,s. If a slot is analytic, reduce the triple index to the double pairing and use the q-radical property to kill its value when paired with the other q-eigenclass; the three-term identity handles an analytic third slot. Thus the functional H↦T_U(F,G;H) factors through [dH]. The degree law gives qT=q²T(F,G;φ*H), so its functional has reciprocal eigenvalue 1/q. The spectrum exclusion forces it to vanish.
targets.title: The q-eigenspace vanishing theorem

targets.name: ColemanWideOpen.colemanFormPairing
targets.statement: Let Ω¹_col,1(U) be the submodule of actual Coleman one-forms generated by G dH for global Coleman G,H with analytic differentials, using the actual Coleman algebra of §3.0b and its multiplication relations. There is a unique k-bilinear pairing P_U:A_col,1(U)×Ω¹_col,1(U)→k with P_U(F,G dH)=T_U(F,G;H). In particular P_U(F,dH)=B_U(F,H). The pairing respects equalities of actual Coleman forms, not only chosen expressions as sums of symbols.

Use the actual Coleman one-form module of §3.0b and symbol/relation theorem of §6.0
No free module on unrelated formal symbols replaces the Coleman form module

tests.name: ColemanWideOpen.colemanFormPairing_2

tests.name: ColemanWideOpen.colemanFormPairing_3
tests.statement: G dH+H dG=d(GH) is one and the same actual form when GH is a Coleman function. Where it lies in the stated module, the two presentations give the same pairing; bilinearity on a free symbol module alone would not prove this.

targets.proofSketch: By §6.2 the generator formula depends on dH, not its primitive constant. §6.0 gives the map Ω¹_col,1→H¹_dR(U)⊗Ω¹(U), G dH↦[dG]⊗dH, and says the kernel of the product presentation is generated inside analytic-function tensors. On those tensors the double-index reduction depends only on the actual product form. Therefore the generator prescription kills all relations and descends; generators prove uniqueness.
targets.title: A pairing on actual Coleman one-forms

targets.name: TateCurve.uniformizationDifferential
targets.title: Tate invariant differential and annular charts
targets.statement: For q∈K× with n=ν_π(q)>0, let u_q:K×/q^ℤ→E_q(K) be the supplied point uniformization. Prove its covering map K×→E_q(K) is locally analytic. Normalize the invariant differential ω_q on E_q by the standard Tate Weierstrass model and prove u_q*ω_q=dz/z. Compare the valuation strips v−1<ν_π(z)<v+1 and connecting annuli v<ν_π(z)<v+1 with the component and annular charts of the regular Tate model. The q-identification gives the final edge. For n=1,2 use loop/parallel-edge charts or a regular subdivision; maps respect coefficient extensions and orientation. This adds differential and chart comparisons to the point theorem, without reconstructing that theorem.

The invariant differential is normalized by the Tate Weierstrass model
Algebraic points and charts over finite extensions use compatible valuation scales
