api.statement: Valuation-strip charts identify the component/end restrictions and the final gluing z↦z/q, also after a compatible regular subdivision.

tests.name: TateCurve.uniformizationDifferential_check1
tests.statement: For q=p³ the last gluing changes log z by −log q, while dlog(z/q)=dz/z.

tests.name: TateCurve.uniformizationDifferential_check2
tests.statement: For n=1 and n=2 the graph has a loop or parallel edges; replacing it by a simple adjacency graph loses the period.

tests.name: TateCurve.uniformizationDifferential_check3
tests.statement: q=1 has n=0 and is excluded. At p=2 all convergent Tate charts and the same differential normalization apply.

targets.proofSketch: Differentiate the convergent Tate coordinate functions of the supplied uniformization to identify the invariant differential, then compare reduction of those coordinates on the valuation strips. Use nodal charts and common refinements for n=1,2. This local analytic comparison proves no equality of natural and Coleman primitives on entire connecting annuli.

targets.name: SingleIntegral.branchTransport
targets.statement: Write the universal single integral of §4.0c as I_univ(a,b;ω)=A+B T in K[T], with T=Log(p). For λ,λ′∈K, I_λ′−I_λ=(λ′−λ)B. For u∈K×, log_λ′(u)−log_λ(u)=(λ′−λ)v_p(u), where v_p(p)=1. For local double or triple indices, changing a branch transports the functions and every auxiliary primitive; the new value is computed by the same residue characterization and the change-of-constant laws. When F and G change by constants A₀,B₀ on a fixed end, ΔB=A₀ Res(dG)−B₀ Res(dF). A branch change with nonconstant valuation term on an annulus is not assumed to be such a constant shift.
hypotheses: p prime, K/ℚ_p finite
Closed regular one-form on a smooth geometrically connected variety, endpoints outside poles
The universal affine-in-T integral is §4.0c
λ and λ′ belong to K; extensions use their images

locator.where: Definition II.1.3 and Theorem II.1.4, p. 74, colmez1998 line 2986; §II.2.5, p. 97, line 3950; index transport from besser-dejeu2012 Lemma 7.4, line 2299

api.name: branchTransport_comp
api.statement: Transport from λ to λ″ is the composite of transport from λ to λ′ and λ′ to λ″, on the full functions and primitive data.

api.name: branchTransport_exact
api.statement: For df the coefficient B is zero; for dlog f it is v_p(f(b)/f(a)).

tests.name: SingleIntegral.branchTransport_1
tests.statement: For u=p, branch change from 0 to 2 changes log(u) by 2; for a ramified uniformizer ϖ with v_p(ϖ)=1/e it changes it by 2/e.

tests.name: SingleIntegral.branchTransport_2
tests.statement: For λ′=λ or ω=0 the change is zero; for u∈O_K×, equivalently v_p(u)=0, the logarithm change is zero, as for u=1. The field unit p∈K× has v_p(p)=1 and changes by 2 when λ=0, λ′=2.

tests.name: SingleIntegral.branchTransport_3
tests.statement: B_e(F+A₀,G+B₀) need not equal B_e(F,G); F=0,G=L,A₀=1,B₀=0 changes it by 1. Index branch independence cannot be inferred from the derivative alone.

targets.proofSketch: Evaluate the affine polynomial at λ′ and λ and subtract. Apply the universal logarithm formula for the multiplicative case. For indices, transport formal/analytic logarithms and products and apply the local characterizations; when the transported changes are constants the explicit constant laws apply. No assertion that arbitrary index data are affine in T is made.
targets.title: Specializing the universal branch

targets.name: SingleIntegral.properHolomorphic_branchIndependent
targets.statement: For a smooth proper geometrically connected curve X/K, a holomorphic one-form ω and algebraic endpoints a,b, its single integral I_λ(a,b;ω) is independent of λ. After a finite extension containing a,b and a temporary basepoint, this is the abelian logarithm on Jac(X) paired with the invariant differential corresponding to ω. Descent eliminates the temporary basepoint; the statement does not require X(K) to be nonempty.
hypotheses: K/ℚ_p finite, all primes
X smooth proper geometrically connected of dimension one
ω regular everywhere; endpoints algebraic over K

locator.where: Lemma II.1.13 and Remark II.1.18, pp. 78–79, colmez1998 line 3147 and line 3213; curve illustration besser-zerbes2017 §3, line 245

api.name: properHolomorphic_universalCoefficient_zero
api.statement: The T coefficient of the universal integral is zero for holomorphic forms on proper curves.

tests.name: SingleIntegral.properHolomorphic_branchIndependent_1
tests.statement: On ℙ¹ all holomorphic one-forms vanish and so do all their integrals.

tests.name: SingleIntegral.properHolomorphic_branchIndependent_2
tests.statement: For an elliptic curve the value from the identity is the unique locally analytic group logarithm with differential ω, and is branch independent.

tests.name: SingleIntegral.properHolomorphic_branchIndependent_3
tests.statement: On the nonproper curve G_m the form dz/z integrates from 1 to p to λ. Properness cannot be dropped.

targets.proofSketch: Use the base Abel–Jacobi and invariant-differential comparison after finite extension. The abelian logarithm is characterized by its differential and group law, independently of a branch. Subtract endpoint values and use finite-extension compatibility; this also removes the choice of the temporary Abel–Jacobi basepoint.
targets.title: Holomorphic integration on a proper curve

targets.name: SingleIntegral.coefficientTrace
targets.statement: For a finite extension L/K of p-adic fields with compatible branches, base change sends I_K(a,b;ω) to I_L(a,b;ω_L). For an L-valued regular closed form ω on U_L and K-rational endpoints a,b, Tr_{L/K}(I_L(a,b;ω))=I_K(a,b;Tr_{L/K}ω), where the form trace uses Ω¹(U_L)=Ω¹(U)⊗_K L. Both identities hold coefficientwise for universal affine polynomials with T fixed. The constructions commute with field embeddings, Galois conjugation and towers.
hypotheses: U/K smooth geometrically connected finite-type algebraic variety
ω regular and closed on U_L; curves may use the complement of their poles
a,b∈U(K) for the trace formula
L/K finite; the branches are restrictions of one branch with parameter in K

locator.where: Theorem II.1.4, p. 74, colmez1998 line 2996; Galois descent Remark 2(iv), pp. 2–3, line 246; trace consequence, not a quoted trace theorem. Compare vologodsky2001 Theorem B(4), line 195, only under p>2

api.name: coefficientTrace_tower
api.statement: Tr_{M/K}I_M=Tr_{L/K}(Tr_{M/L}I_M) in every finite tower M/L/K, with the same coefficient trace on forms.

api.name: singleIntegral_galois
api.statement: σ(I(a,b;ω))=I(σa,σb;σω), with σ fixing the universal T.

api.name: primitive_galois_average
api.statement: After a finite Galois extension containing a point a, averaging the conjugates of P↦I(a,P;ω) gives a K-defined primitive torsor representative; any two such representatives differ by a K-constant.

tests.name: SingleIntegral.coefficientTrace_1
tests.statement: If ω is defined over K and [L:K]=n, Tr(I_L(a,b;ω))=n I_K(a,b;ω), not I_K(a,b;ω).

tests.name: SingleIntegral.coefficientTrace_2
tests.statement: L=K is identity, and a=b gives zero. Every finite extension of p-adic fields is separable, including ramified quadratic extensions at p=2.

tests.name: SingleIntegral.coefficientTrace_3
tests.statement: Trace is not multiplicative: for α²=π in a quadratic extension, Tr(α)=0 but Tr(α²)=2π≠0. Do not trace each factor of an index separately.

targets.proofSketch: Finite scalar extension of forms and K-linearity reduce the coefficient trace formula to ω=αη with η over K. Trace linearity and the base-change identity then prove it. Equivalently sum over embeddings in a normal closure using the pinned embedding formula and descend. The pinned tower theorem gives transitivity. Average over the finite Galois group, dividing by its nonzero order, to obtain a descended primitive; its constant ambiguity follows from the natural theory.
targets.title: Finite extension and coefficient trace

targets.name: Curve.divisorSingleIntegral
targets.statement: For a smooth proper geometrically connected curve X/K, meromorphic ω, and a degree-zero K-divisor D=Σ_x n_x[x] disjoint from its poles, choose a finite Galois extension L splitting the support and containing a point a outside the poles. Define ∫_D ω=Σ_x n_x Σ_{σ:κ(x)→L} I_L(a,σx;ω). Its value is independent of a, L and the embeddings used to display the geometric support, belongs to K and is additive in D and K-linear in ω. Degree means Σ_x n_x[κ(x):K]=0. No K-rational basepoint is part of the exported object.
hypotheses: K/ℚ_p finite, any prime, fixed branch
X smooth proper geometrically connected curve
D integral divisor of degree zero; support disjoint from poles of ω
L is a finite Galois extension splitting the support and containing a permissible temporary point

locator.where: Degree-zero divisor evaluation and splitting argument, §2, p. 4, besser-zerbes2017 line 142; Galois consequence of colmez1998 Remark 2(iv), line 246

api.name: divisorSingleIntegral_split
api.statement: For D=b−a with a,b rational, the value is I_K(a,b;ω).

api.name: divisorSingleIntegral_ext
api.statement: Equal divisors, evaluated as finite sums over closed points, give equal values; regrouping the support changes nothing.

api.name: divisorSingleIntegral_add
api.statement: The evaluation is a homomorphism on divisors of degree zero disjoint from the pole support.

api.name: divisorSingleIntegral_baseChange
api.statement: Ordinary divisor pullback to a finite field extension preserves the value after scalar extension; closed points split with their usual multiplicities.

tests.name: Curve.divisorSingleIntegral_1
tests.statement: For α²=π in a ramified quadratic extension, D=[t²−π]−2[0] on ℙ¹ and ω=t dt give ∫_D ω=π, since each geometric point contributes π/2. This works at p=2 as a field identity.

tests.name: Curve.divisorSingleIntegral_2
tests.statement: D=0 gives zero even when X(K) is empty; changing the temporary basepoint contributes deg(D) times one integral, hence zero.

tests.name: Curve.divisorSingleIntegral_3
tests.statement: A single quadratic closed point has degree 2, not 1. Subtracting one rational point does not make degree zero and the putative evaluation depends on the basepoint.

targets.proofSketch: Chasles makes a basepoint change contribute deg(D)·I(a′,a;ω)=0. Scalar extension and a common finite Galois overfield compare any two splitting fields. Galois equivariance permutes the geometric points and changes the basepoint only, so the scalar is fixed and lies in K. Finite-sum linearity gives the API.
targets.title: Degree-zero divisors without a rational basepoint

targets.name: Curve.tracedLocalIndexSum
targets.statement: For X/K smooth proper geometrically connected and a finite reduced Z, use K-defined primitive representatives from §7.3 for ω,η regular off Z. At a closed point x the formal germs lie over κ(x); define its double contribution as Tr_{κ(x)/K} B_x(F,G), and sum over Z. This sum is independent of the two global primitive constants and extends the corrected pairing to nonsplit poles. For triple-index data that themselves descend to κ(x), define the local traced contribution Tr_{κ(x)/K} T_x(F,G;H) with the full auxiliary data. No auxiliary independence is asserted for a local triple index. For any expression already defined over K, extension to L followed by scalar trace multiplies its value by [L:K]. For a finite Galois-stable family of annular ends with end fields κ(e), define the corresponding end-sums by Σ_e Tr_{κ(e)/K} B_e or Σ_e Tr_{κ(e)/K} T_e, using descended functions and, for triples, the full compatible auxiliary data. Their scalar extension is the sum over geometric ends.
hypotheses: K/ℚ_p finite; a compatible branch
Z finite reduced, all residue fields finite separable over K
F,G are descended representatives of the global single-integral primitive torsors
For a traced triple contribution, functions and auxiliary primitives are all defined over κ(x)

locator.where: Galois descent Remark 2(iv), line 246, and §II.2.5, line 3950; consequence of besser2017 Definition 3.4/Corollary 5.3, lines 435/807 and besser-dejeu2012 §8, line 2524

api.name: tracedLocalIndexSum_split
api.statement: In a normal splitting extension the embedded traced contribution is the sum of the conjugate point contributions, and the global sum equals the split corrected pairing.

api.name: tracedLocalIndexSum_tower
api.statement: Computing residue traces through an intermediate residue field gives the same contribution.

api.name: tracedLocalIndexSum_congr
api.statement: Parameter changes preserving the formal point orientation and equal local germs preserve the traced values.

api.name: tracedLocalIndexSum_bilinear
api.statement: The global double sum is alternating and K-bilinear in the forms; it factors through de Rham classes and extends the proper cup product after descent.

api.name: tracedEndIndexSum
api.statement: Taking the index over each end field and then its field trace gives the same scalar as splitting all ends and summing their conjugate contributions; traces compose in towers.

tests.name: Curve.tracedLocalIndexSum_1
tests.statement: At the quadratic closed point t²−π=0, B_x(1,log(t²−π))=1 over κ(x), so its trace is 2; at infinity the residue is −2, and the global constant-first sum is 0.

tests.name: Curve.tracedLocalIndexSum_2
tests.statement: A K-rational point uses the identity trace; an empty point set contributes zero for global regular forms.

tests.name: Curve.tracedLocalIndexSum_3
tests.statement: In a quadratic extension α²=π, replacing Tr(B) by a product of traces of its input coefficients can turn Tr(α²)=2π into 0. Only the whole scalar index is traced.

targets.proofSketch: Scalar extension of local indices and the pinned trace-as-embeddings identity identify each closed-point contribution with its geometric conjugate sum. Apply §4.4 after splitting. Faithful scalar embedding proves constant independence, cohomology factorization and cup compatibility over K. Transitivity is the pinned trace tower theorem. For triple data the same proof yields descent of values, retaining local choice dependence.
targets.title: Closed-point indices and traced sums

targets.name: Curve.integrationRealization_descent
targets.statement: For every smooth proper geometrically connected X/K, every meromorphic ω and every degree-zero divisor away from its poles, choose any finite extension giving a split regular nodal model with separated pole and divisor support. The harmonic formula of §§4.2–4.3 evaluates the single integral of §4.0c and §7.4, and the corrected double formula evaluates §7.5. These values agree after any further coefficient extension, common model refinement, node subdivision or pole separation, hence descend to the original arbitrary-reduction curve. For a connected Coleman wide open with F,G,H and global compatible auxiliary data defined over K, T_U and P_U are K-valued and commute with scalar extension and admissible shrinking. This last assertion is about a wide open; it does not construct a triple pairing of three arbitrary whole-curve Vologodsky primitives by summing components. A connected wide open whose constant field is a finite extension k₀/K is treated over k₀, and its K-valued end-sum is the field trace, equivalently the sum over geometric components.
hypotheses: K/ℚ_p finite, p any prime; fixed branch parameter in K
X/K smooth proper geometrically connected curve; no reduction or genus restriction
Meromorphic forms evaluated off poles; divisor degree zero where a divisor is evaluated
Triple assertions require actual global Coleman wide-open data and descended auxiliary choices

locator.where: Corollary 1.2 and §2 finite-extension argument, p. 3, besser-zerbes2017 line 95 and line 130; besser2017 Proposition 4.12(3), line 753; besser-dejeu2012 introduction p. 310, line 250

api.name: integrationRealization_commonExtension
api.statement: Two realization fields and models are compared in one common finite extension with compatible generic-fibre identifications.

api.name: integrationRealization_divisor
api.statement: The harmonic evaluation equals the K-valued degree-zero divisor integral without a chosen K-point.

api.name: wideOpenIndex_galoisDescent
api.statement: If the wide-open functions and auxiliary data descend, their end-sums are fixed by Galois and belong to the coefficient field; local end values may require their residue fields.

tests.name: Curve.integrationRealization_descent_1
tests.statement: Good reduction uses a single component and gives Coleman integration, with no graph correction.

tests.name: Curve.integrationRealization_descent_2
tests.statement: A ramified extension splitting a quadratic divisor gives the value π of §7.4 and traced local residue 2 of §7.5, independent of further ramification.

tests.name: Curve.integrationRealization_descent_3
tests.statement: A whole-curve sum of local triple indices changes under unrelated component auxiliary shifts by the residue change laws. Wide-open global-choice independence does not certify that construction.

tests.name: wideOpen_larger_constant_field
tests.statement: A connected wide open with quadratic constant field L has K-valued end-sum Tr_{L/K} of its L-valued sum; the scalar 1 contributes 2, not 1. Geometric connectedness cannot be inferred from connectedness alone.

targets.proofSketch: StableReduction supplies finite nodal reduction in all genera, regularization, splitting of branches and separation of marked sections, together with common refinements. Apply the split comparison and then §7.3. Since each harmonic evaluation equals the intrinsic natural integral of §4.0c, two realizations agree in a common field; trace/embedding descent gives the K-value. §1.3 handles the metric under refinement, and §7.5 handles nonsplit local terms. For global triple data use §5.5 and §6.2 and descend the resulting scalar, without asserting a new global bad-reduction triple construction.
targets.title: Independence of semistable extensions and models

targets.name: TateCurve.singleIntegral_normalization
targets.statement: For a Tate curve E_q/K with q∈K× and n=ν_π(q)>0, the invariant differential dz/z has primitive on K×/q^ℤ given by F(z)=log_λ(z)−(ν_π(z)/n)log_λ(q), normalized by F(1)=0. In the regular n-gon presentation its cyclic harmonic jump is −log_λ(q)/n. For n=1 use the loop presentation and for n=2 the two parallel edges, or a compatible regular subdivision. The expression is invariant under z↦qz and under a change of logarithm branch.
hypotheses: K/ℚ_p finite, fixed uniformizer π and any logarithm branch
q≠0, ν_π(q)=n>0; this hypothesis makes n invertible in K
The point-level Tate uniformization is supplied by EllipticCurves Layer 4; its differential normalization is §7.0
Algebraic points are interpreted after compatible finite coefficient extension

locator.where: §3, pp. 5–6, besser-zerbes2017 line 245 and line 265

api.name: TateCurve.singleIntegral_q_periodic
api.statement: F(qz)−F(z)=log(q)−(n/n)log(q)=0.

api.name: TateCurve.singleIntegral_branch
api.statement: The branch change is (λ′−λ)(v_p(z)−ν_π(z)v_p(q)/n)=0 since v_p=ν_π/e.

tests.name: TateCurve.singleIntegral_normalization_1
tests.statement: Over ℚ_p take π=p, q=p³ and log(p)=1. Then n=3, every cyclic jump is −1 and F(z)=log(z)−ν_π(z); enforcing zero jumps fails.

tests.name: TateCurve.singleIntegral_normalization_2
tests.statement: For n=1 or n=2 the same formula holds on loops or parallel edges. The case q=1 is excluded because n=0 and the quotient is not this Tate curve.

tests.name: TateCurve.singleIntegral_normalization_3
tests.statement: At p=2 the cancellation uses only characteristic-zero division by n and v_p=ν_π/e; it imposes no odd-prime condition.

targets.proofSketch: On successive fundamental annuli use log(z) as the Coleman primitive. Crossing the final q-identification contributes −log(q). Project this cochain to the constant cyclic harmonic cochain, using §1.2. Subtract the vertex potential and apply §4.3. The displayed two-term computations verify q-periodicity and branch independence.
targets.title: A cycle with nonzero jump and branch cancellation

layers.examples: A ramified quadratic closed point tests residue-field traces; a degree-zero divisor tests basepoint cancellation; the Tate curve tests branch cancellation with a nonzero cycle.
layers.dependencies: All previous layers; the universal single-integration theorem of §4.0c; StableReduction Layers 0–1, 4–5, 7 and 9; finite-dimensional field trace at the pins. No regulator construction is used.

suppliers.what: Analytic Laurent and logarithmic carriers, residues, branches, analytic primitive and constant-kernel theorems; good-reduction Coleman algebra, algebraic coefficient extension and integral, with strict-neighborhood and same-reduction pullback hypotheses. Natural arbitrary-reduction integration and extra comparisons are targets here.

Complete field extension, reduction, classical rigid spaces with discs/annuli and gluing, quasi-separated base change, and algebraic analytification. These sections do not supply Coleman integration, wide-open reciprocity or the curve cohomology comparison.

Finite DVR extensions and common refinements; nodal charts, split branches and dual graphs with loops; curve positivity; regularization and common model resolutions; all-genus finite-extension nodal reduction; separation of marked sections.

Proper curves are projective; Jacobian and Picard degree/divisor interface; abelian-variety carrier; pointed Abel–Jacobi and base change after a temporary splitting extension. No unpointed Abel–Jacobi morphism is assumed; the extra natural and topology bridge is target 4.0e.
Tate curve for q a unit with |q|<1 and its point-level, finite-extension and Galois-compatible uniformization; the analytic invariant-differential comparison is target 7.0.

abelianLog.add, abelianLog.derivative, abelianLog.unique, abelianLog.baseChange, abelianLog.functorial and abelianLog.cp for abelian varieties over finite K/ℚ_p, with arbitrary reduction. The cp theorem extends the points of the same K-defined variety; arbitrary ℂ_p-defined varieties and finite-model agreement are target 4.0. Its colemanAbelian.integral comparison assumes good reduction; the additional natural comparison is target 4.0e.
Smooth projective compactification of a smooth quasi-projective characteristic-zero variety, used on a dense open in target 4.0b; no new resolution construction.

Finite rigid coefficient extension, the component dagger/rigid and proper tube comparisons, finite dimensionality, linear Q_K-Frobenius for Q_K=#κ_K and identity coefficient lift, its positive iterates q=Q_K^r, and linearFrobenius_baseChange (residue extension of degree f uses the f-th iterate), proper weight one, curve Gysin and affine-curve weights (boundary q times roots of unity). Only the additional semistable curve Čech/graph and index/cup comparisons are built here.
